summary: Daemon-only change in packages/daemon: (1) accept the new `receipt_timeout` exception reason and treat it as 'slow, not gone' when the process is alive; (2) bound and de-duplicate the alive-architect re-send path with an in-memory ledger (three re-sends, pauses 5 s/15 s/45 s, each re-send carrying the original dedupe key in the listener publish body, one cap log line); (3) publish `worker-queued` once per enqueue and only for architect assignments, never for daemon catch-ups. No daemon/plugin contract bump, no state schema change, no smoke rig (spec acceptance line 6 is withdrawn).

contract.fixedByParent: dispatch://LEGION-101/spec, section Design. Do not renegotiate. Exception reasons on `notifications.envoy.exceptions.notifications.role.<token>`: `no_holder`, `delivery_failed`, `receipt_timeout` (new; emitted by LEGION-108's listener). Exception payload keeps `original_topic`, `event_id`, `payload`, `dedupe_key`, `reason` (see `deliveryExceptionPayload`, packages/envoy/cmd/listener/delivery.go:91-100). Listener publish API `POST /v1/messages/publish` gains an optional `dedupe_key` body field, used verbatim as the envelope's dedupe key, mutually exclusive with `idempotency_key` (LEGION-108 lands it; today's listener decodes with a non-strict `json.NewDecoder` (api.go:299) so it ignores the field and mints a fresh key — the daemon sends it now regardless).
facts: The listener mints a fresh `event_id` for EVERY publish (`messageEnvelope`, api.go:127) and the exception's `event_id` is the failed envelope's (`publishDeliveryException`, delivery.go:113). A re-sent copy's failure therefore never carries the original event id. Only `dedupe_key` (once LEGION-108 lands) and the verbatim `original_topic`+`payload` (always) survive across a chain.

The exception lane is core NATS, handled concurrently by the pump (`track(handleMessage(...))`, events.ts:975), never serialized: a long wait inside `handleException` blocks nothing else, and `EventPump.drain()` (awaited at shutdown after `processManager.dispose()`, index.ts:611/628) waits for it — so the wait must be cancellable from `dispose()`.

`ensureController()` for an alive controller only manages its registration deadline (processes.ts:1922-1931) — it re-sends nothing, so the controller branch of `handleException` stays as it is for every reason.

decisions.decision: The re-send ledger is keyed by the message itself — `original.topic + '\n' + original.payload` — not by `event_id`, and the re-send carries the dedupe key the triggering exception reported (`original.dedupeKey`).
decisions.why: A per-event-id ledger counts to 1 per chain in production (see contract.facts[0]): the unit test would pass while the loop continued. Keying by `dedupe_key` bounds the chain only once LEGION-108's listener is deployed (an older listener mints a fresh dedupe key per re-send); keying by topic+payload bounds it in every deploy order, which is the parent's stated property ("any one of the three fixes alone stops the loop"). The daemon re-sends `original.payload` verbatim, so the key is stable by construction. Cost: two byte-identical messages to one role that BOTH fail delivery within RESEND_LEDGER_TTL_MS share one three-re-send budget (each re-send still carries its own exception's dedupe key, so the plugin's dedupe never conflates them). This is not the parent's rejected 'receiver dedupes by payload text': no delivery is dropped, only the recovery budget is shared.
decisions.specEdit: The spec's Design bullet for processes.ts and the ledger 'New since we talked' bullet were updated in place to this rule (version summary 'plan: ledger keyed by message, not event id'); acceptance line 3's 'a different event id starts its own count' now reads 'a different message starts its own count'.

decisions.decision: Every re-send, including the first, is preceded by its pause: exception k (k = 1..3) for a chain waits RESEND_PAUSES_MS[k-1] (5 s, 15 s, 45 s) and then re-probes, directs, and re-publishes. A fourth exception logs the cap line and drops the entry; nothing is sent.
decisions.why: Spec: three re-sends and three pauses, 'spaced by the three pauses on the injected clock'. With an older listener a `delivery_failed` on an alive holder is almost always a busy holder; waiting 5 s before the first copy lets its turn end. For a genuinely lost claim (`no_holder` after a listener restart, LEGION-29) a 5 s delay before the reclaim directive is harmless.

decisions.decision: An exception for a chain whose re-send pause is still running is dropped with one log line and NOT counted; `settle()` after the re-send fires releases the chain for the next exception.
decisions.why: This is the parent Design's 'next-allowed time': only the re-send in flight can produce the chain's next legitimate exception. Without it two near-simultaneous exceptions would spend two of the three attempts on one copy.

decisions.decision: Probe BEFORE consulting the ledger (a dead root is resurrected at once, exactly as today, for every reason) and AGAIN after the pause (alive -> `controlDirective`; dead -> `resurrect`).
decisions.why: Spec requirement: behaviour for a process that probes dead is unchanged. A root that dies during a 45 s pause would otherwise get a `natsRequest` that times out or nacks, and a nack publishes a misleading `revive-failed` to the controller.

decisions.decision: The `reclaim-architect` directive JSON sent over `legion.ctl.<tree>.<generation>` keeps exactly `{type, issue, redeliver:{topic,payload,eventId}}`; the dedupe key travels as a separate argument to `controlDirective` and on to `publishRole`, never inside the directive.
decisions.why: Spec: no contract bump. The plugin's `parseControlDirective` (packages/pi-envoy/src/legion/control.ts:36-65) would tolerate an extra field, but the shape is part of what 'no bump' promises. Build `redeliver` by destructuring `{topic, payload, eventId}` from `exception.original` — assigning the whole object would leak `dedupeKey` into the JSON (TypeScript's excess-property check does not fire on a variable).

decisions.decision: For a phase worker or sub-architect, 'alive' on `receipt_timeout` means: the claim has a locator AND (`this.workerClients.has(token)` — a cached shim client; a closed one is evicted by `onWorkerClientClosed` — OR `this.probeLocator(claim.locator, token)` answers `alive`). Anything else (no locator, dead pane) takes the existing `resumeWorker` path.
decisions.why: Matches the assignment ('cached shim client is connected / its locator probes alive'). The pane probe is a `list-panes` plus `/proc` start-ticks check with no side effects; dialing the socket would cache a client as a side effect of a log-only decision. A probe throw is caught by `handleException`'s existing catch (logged once, nothing cleared) — the spec's Errors row.

tasks.title: resend-ledger.ts: the in-memory re-send ledger
change: Export the constants with one comment block: `RESEND_PAUSES_MS = [5_000, 15_000, 45_000] as const` (pause before re-send k; chosen so a holder busy for about a minute sees at most three copies, the last one after it is likely idle — spec 'New since we talked'; constants, not configuration: nobody tunes them), `MAX_RESENDS = RESEND_PAUSES_MS.length`, `RESEND_LEDGER_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000` (an entry no exception has touched for this long is forgotten: the exception for a re-sent copy arrives within seconds of the re-send — the listener's 2 s receipt window — so five minutes of silence means the chain ended in delivery; bounds the map without a timer).
`export class ResendLedger` with `constructor(now: () => number)`; entries `Map<string, { attempts: number; inFlight: boolean; touchedAt: number }>`.

`claim(key: string): { kind: "resend"; attempt: number; pauseMs: number } | { kind: "in-flight" } | { kind: "capped"; attempts: number }` — first prunes every entry with `now - touchedAt > RESEND_LEDGER_TTL_MS`; absent -> create `{attempts: 1, inFlight: true}` and return attempt 1 / 5 s; present and `inFlight` -> `in-flight` (not counted, `touchedAt` refreshed); present and `attempts >= MAX_RESENDS` -> delete the entry, return `capped`; else `attempts += 1`, `inFlight = true`, return that attempt and `RESEND_PAUSES_MS[attempts - 1]`.

`settle(key)`: `inFlight = false`, `touchedAt = now()` (called once the re-send has fired — or the chain was abandoned because the process was dead/disposed, so the next exception is not misread as in flight). `clear()`: empties the map (called from `ProcessManager.dispose()`).
The chain key is built by the caller (`ProcessManager`): `${original.topic}\n${original.payload}` — see decisions D1. The ledger never stores payloads beyond the key string and never logs them.
tests: L1 resend-ledger.test.ts 'claims three attempts with pauses 5 s, 15 s, 45 s, then reports capped and drops the entry': with a fixed `now`, claim/settle three times asserting `{attempt: 1, pauseMs: 5000}`, `{attempt: 2, pauseMs: 15000}`, `{attempt: 3, pauseMs: 45000}`; the fourth claim is `{kind: "capped", attempts: 3}`; a fifth claim (same key) is attempt 1 again (entry dropped).
L2 'reports in-flight without counting until settle': claim -> claim again is `in-flight`; settle; claim is attempt 2 (not 3).

L3 'forgets an entry idle past RESEND_LEDGER_TTL_MS but keeps a fresh one': key A claimed and settled at t0, key B claimed and settled at t0 + TTL/2; with `now` at t0 + TTL + 1, a claim on A is attempt 1 (forgotten) and a claim on B is attempt 2 (kept).

L4 'keeps independent counts per key': interleaved claims on two keys each count from 1 (also covered by P6's last step; keep whichever the implementer finds less redundant — L4 may be folded into L1).
